preconditions.description: The input integer k is between 1 and 10^9 inclusive.

postconditions.description: The output graph has n vertices where n is between 2 and 1000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: len(matrix) == n and all(len(row) == n for row in matrix)
postconditions.description: The output contains an n x n adjacency matrix.

postconditions.expression: all(cell in ('N', 'Y') for row in matrix for cell in row)
postconditions.description: Every element in the adjacency matrix is either 'N' or 'Y'.
The graph is simple: no self-loops exist (diagonal elements are 'N').

postconditions.expression: all(matrix[i][j] == matrix[j][i] for i in range(n) for j in range(n))
postconditions.description: The graph is undirected: the adjacency matrix is symmetric.
The number of shortest paths between vertex 1 and vertex 2 in the constructed graph is exactly k.
There exists at least one path between vertex 1 and vertex 2.
